newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end sharply up on weather concerns.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end sharply up on weather concerns.

text.p: Concern that a bout of dry weather in the central U.S. Midwest could stunt the development of the soybean crop boosted futures to sharply higher closes Monday, traders and analysts said.
"The key is that we seem to have missed the rain and it looks like it's going to be warm through Wednesday and Thursday," said Jerry Gidel, analyst with Dean Witter.
The concerns caused some soybean contracts to rally the daily 30-cent trading limit throughout the session.
Some meteorologists had forecast rain for the weekend in the Midwest, but the rain that fell missed the dry areas, which span from eastern Iowa to western Indiana, Gidel said.

With temperatures climbing into the 90s (degrees Fahrenheit), the corn crop is seen as even more vulnerable to high heat and dry weather than soybeans, as corn enters the critical pollination stage, traders and analysts said.
In fact, many traders expect the U.S. Department of Agriculture to show improvement in the soybean crop when the agency releases crop reports at 1500 CDT.
August soybeans ended 29 cent per bushel higher at $7.79 a bushel and other months were up 24 to 33-1/4 cents, with limitless July up the most.

The market disregarded export shipment data that fell at the low end of expectations. The U.S. Department of Agriculture reported shipments of 4.716 million bushels. That figure was below expectations for five to eight million bushels.
Many see the market as poised for additional sharp gains if the weather remains dry. Commodity funds hold very large short positions, so heavy short covering was expected by some.

On the day, Prudential Securities bought 11 million bushels August, Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought four million January and Refco bought three million November. USA Trading sold 3.5 million bushels November, traders said.
In options trade, Smith Barney bought 1,000 September $6.75 calls and Term Commodities sold 800 August $8.25 calls, floor sources said.
Volatility in August closed at 48-1/2 percent, up from 41-1/2 on Thursday. November closed at 23-1/2 percent, up from 22-1/2 percent on Thursday.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 64,000 contracts. That figure compared with Friday's actual volume of 47,850 contracts.
